messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: Paging oncall: high error-rate detected for ALB/NLB fronting apac1 cluster (region apac1). automatic alert: 5xx spike + connection resets. Severity: P1.
Sam: I'm on it. seeing 502/504s from edge. rate jumped ~04:12 UTC.
Priya: Confirming from Synthetics: curl to /health returns 200 from eu clients but 502 from apac.
Jordan: Logs from ingress show a lot of ECONNRESET and upstream timeout messages. snippet: `envoy error upstream reset, reason: connection failure, code: 104`
Liam: Incident bot shows recent DNS changes? NOC-Bot: No Route53 changes in last 24h.
Sam: Checking ALB target health: some targets in apac1b flapping Unhealthy -> Healthy -> Unhealthy. healthcheck failure: tcp timeout.
Priya: Running quick tcpdump on one ingress pod (apac1b): lots of retransmits and duplicate ACKs.
Sam: Could be noisy NIC/ENI in apac1b. Opening cloud console now.
NOC-Bot: Notified cloud provider support ticket #CP-99812 at 04:25 UTC.
Jordan: Quick mitigation proposal: 1) remove apac1b from ALB target group 2) increase NLB target keepalive to avoid short conn resets 3) scale ingress controller replicas in apac1a/c. Thoughts?
Liam: +1 to removing the unhealthy AZ from rotation for now. Do we have weighted routing via Route53 to shift traffic?
Sam: We're on weighted DNS for some customers, but most traffic goes through ALB. I'll deregister targets in apac1b now.
Sam: command: `aws elbv2 deregister-targets --target-group-arn arn:aws:tg:apac1:... --targets Id=i-0123abcd...`
Priya: After deregistering apac1b targets, 5xx rate dropped ~60% within 90s. Metrics: errors from 24% -> 9%.
Jordan: Scaling ingress controller to 3 replicas in apac1a and apac1c: `kubectl scale deploy ingress-controller -n ingress --replicas=3`
Liam: Patches applied to keepalive settings on NLB (in place config change): `aws elbv2 modify-load-balancer-attributes --load-balancer-arn arn:aws:nlb:... --attributes Key=proxy_protocol_v2.enabled,Value=false` (note: config example).
Sam: Also toggled cross-zone load balancing off temporarily to avoid cross-AZ persist connection weirdness.
Priya: Customer impact: roughly 8% of global requests experienced elevated error rates for ~35 minutes concentrated on apac cluster. No data-plane data loss reported; retries satisfied most requests.
Jordan: Observed symptomatic stack traces for a small subset of requests: `upstream read error: broken pipe` and `connect timeout`.
Liam: Rolling redeploy of the ingress nodes in apac1b is queued; but until cloud provider responds, we've left the AZ out of rotation.
Sam: Oncall handoff plan: I'll lead mitigation now and hand off to Priya at 05:30 UTC for follow-ups and cloud-provider coordination.
incident-bot: Note: this thread was escalated to ENG-SRE and ENG-INFRA. page history: pages sent to oncall at 04:14 UTC, escalation to ENG-SRE at 04:20 UTC.
Priya: Running a more detailed packet capture and sending to CP support. evidence attached: tcpdump sample + pcap link (internal).
Jordan: Quick customer comms draft: "We're investigating increased 5xx from apac region; traffic is being shifted to healthy AZs; mitigation in progress; updates every 30 minutes."
Sam: I'll post that to status.redwood and add note to customers impacted via support.
Liam: Cloud provider replied (initial): "We see ENI detach/attach flapping in apac1b associated with host-level networking issue; escalating internally." timestamped 04:42 UTC.
Priya: Post-mitigation metrics: error rate back to baseline in apac after removing AZ and scaling controllers. We'll keep the AZ out of rotation and schedule a controlled green/blue to validate.
Jordan: Anything else urgent? we should run a canary test to ensure no regression before reintroducing AZ.
Sam: Agreed. canary curl loop to the withdrawn AZ shows successful responses only after full node reattach by provider — until then keep out.
Priya: Customer impact assessment: approx 12k requests failed (retriable) for impacted customers; SLA exposure limited due to retries and multi-AZ fallback.
Liam: Filing follow-up ticket to infra: investigate NLB idle timeout and ALB healthcheck sensitivity for flaky AZs.
Sam: Handoff reminder: Priya takes oncall at 05:30 UTC. I'll update runbook and handoff notes.
Priya: Taking over. leaving the AZ out of rotation and monitoring. next update 05:00 UTC or earlier if cloud provides root cause.
NOC-Bot: Cloud provider support updated: "Investigating host NIC driver; ETA for next update 2 hours."
Sam: Closing immediate mitigation loop. Final note for thread: mitigation reduced customer-facing errors; root cause suspected noisy host networking in apac1b; follow-up with cloud provider required before reintroducing AZ.
Priya: :white_check_mark: Handoff complete.
